definition: The process of identifying, documenting, and prioritizing the features and capabilities needed in a software solution.
extendedDefinition: Requirements gathering is the disciplined process of identifying, documenting, and prioritizing what a software solution must do, and it is the foundation of every successful purchase. Well-gathered requirements prevent the two most common failures: buying too much capability that never gets used, and missing a critical need discovered only after deployment. The process starts with stakeholders and users describing real workflows, then converts those descriptions into concrete functional and non-functional requirements, such as performance, security, and compliance conditions. Requirements should be prioritized into must-have, should-have, and nice-to-have tiers so that trade-offs during vendor comparison are guided by agreed criteria rather than impulse. Documented requirements also serve negotiation and implementation, since vendors can respond with precision and acceptance testing can confirm delivery. Teams that invest in gathering requirements early consistently shorten evaluation cycles and avoid costly rework.
